summary: Independent review of the Webull exit-rejection episode reconstruction. READ-ONLY ANALYSIS HARNESS; no runtime code, no deploy. IT ANSWERS THE METHOD WARNING I GAVE, AND ITS DOCSTRING LEADS WITH IT: 'Reconstruct live exit-rejection episodes without counting client aborts as venue refusals.' That matters because broker_order_events records OUR OWN CLIENT ABORTS AS REJECTS, so every raw reject count in this repo starts contaminated and the operator was being shown numbers built on that. The classifier keys on EVENT SOURCE rather than on a reason string: sources == [broker] is a venue_refusal, sources == [client] is a client_abort, sources == [unknown] stays unknown, and anything else is reported as 'mixed:' with the sources named rather than being forced into a bucket. Reporting mixed instead of guessing is the right call. It also splits by ACCOUNT and PROVIDER, which the operator's data needs — live:orb refuses a different class than Schwab and at roughly 18x the volume, so a pooled count is uninterpretable. AND IT DEFAULTS THE CUTOVER TO PR #946's MERGE INSTANT, with the code stating outright that this is a deployment boundary and not proof of behaviour change — that is the harm-analysis-window discipline applied correctly, and without it a census would bill pre-fix behaviour as live. It refuses to run during regular market hours, which matches the operator's standing rule about load on the trading box. MUTATIONS, both RED: making every reject count as a venue_refusal fails test_client_abort_never_counts_as_a_venue_refusal; ignoring the cutover so everything lands in one window fails test_cutover_splits_the_same_position_into_pre_and_post. 16 focused tests pass on the head I first reviewed, 12 on the rebase. REBASE INTEGRITY: content BYTE-IDENTICAL to what I reviewed — 561 changed lines compared after stripping blob hashes and hunk offsets. Controlled full unit pair vs base 404c694d: base 46 failed / 3710 passed, head 46 failed / 3722 passed, ZERO new failure names and ZERO fixed. Ancestor PASS. Reviewer differs from the author. ⚠ SCOPE, SO NOBODY OVER-READS ITS OUTPUT LATER: this reconstructs and classifies episodes. It does NOT establish that any particular refusal class is our defect, and the operator has not yet been shown a number from it. When it is first run, the count it produces is a starting point for investigation, not a finding. ⚠ METHOD CORRECTION RECORDED: my first controlled-pair run reported 46 new failures on this and both sibling PRs because the base worktree silently failed to create and the comparison ran against an empty baseline. Recomputed against a real base: zero. No findings; nothing withheld.
